extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, trademark/non-patent practitioners, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) / legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: explains service/notice procedures, effect of non-response, the imposed suspension/probation and conditions for reinstatement, and OED/USPTO enforcement options. Targets how the USPTO applies disciplinary standards when a state disciplinary order exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed where a practitioner 'has been suspended on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the State'—i.e., violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order was predicated on the California Supreme Court's suspension (In re Francis Hotchkiss Lewis, Jr., Case No. S192797). Reciprocal discipline can be identical to discipline imposed by the state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice procedures (mail and publication under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24, 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be mailed by certified mail to the respondent at the last address known to the OED Director; if mailing is returned unclaimed, service may be effected by publication in the Official Gazette per 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.35.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order gave the respondent 40 days to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline and provided directions on how to request copies of the Notice and supporting documents. Publication in the Official Gazette must inform the respondent how to obtain documents and how to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, the OED Director may determine there is 'no genuine issue of material fact' and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, more than forty days elapsed after publication with no request for documents or response, and the Director determined reciprocal discipline appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and probation terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was suspended from practice before the USPTO for two years and placed on probation for two years, both starting on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies suspension applies to the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility and conditions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60; restitution requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may request reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after serving a minimum of nine months of the two-year USPTO suspension and only after having made restitution to specified clients in accordance with the state court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reinstatement is granted by the OED Director, the respondent may practice patent law (and trademark/non-patent law subject to additional conditions) during the remainder of the probationary period, provided the respondent is not subsequently suspended or excluded from practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for practicing trademark and non-patent law during probation (37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition for reinstatement is granted, respondent may practice trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO during the remainder of probation only if the respondent 'otherwise satisfies the conditions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.14(a) conditions (e.g., evidence of rehabilitation, compliance with state licensing conditions) must be met; the Final Order ties reinstatement for trademark/non-patent practice to satisfying § 11.14(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director enforcement during probation — Order to Show Cause and additional suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule during the two-year probation, the Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the respondent's last address of record, and grant fifteen days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After considering any response, if the Director remains of the opinion the respondent failed to comply, the Director may deliver the Order to Show Cause and supporting materials to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to an additional fifteen months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative enforcement if respondent not yet reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is not required to pursue the paragraph 5 actions (Order to Show Cause / immediate suspension) if the respondent has not yet been reinstated; instead the Director may consider alleged noncompliance in connection with any reinstatement request and/or seek discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34–11.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the OED Director discretion to treat alleged violations either as grounds for denying reinstatement or to initiate separate disciplinary proceedings under the broader disciplinary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of suspension notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette detailing the respondent's suspension, probation, the rule(s) violated, restitution and reinstatement conditions, and the underlying state court action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample notice in the Order includes specific content: respondent's name, registration number, nature and length of suspension/probation, violated federal and state rules, restitution requirement, references to statutory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24), and where OED disciplinary decisions are publicly posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct supporting discipline (state rules and misappropriation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disciplinary action was predicated on specific findings by the California Supreme Court: representing clients without informed written consent in potential conflicts (rule 3-310(C)(1)); entering aggregate settlements without informed written consent (rule 3-310(D)); failing to render appropriate accounts (rule 4-100(B)(3)); failing to promptly resolve a dispute before disbursing funds (rule 4-100(B)(4)); trust account shortfall (rule 4-100(A)); and misappropriation of client funds (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites misappropriation of at least $7,687.84 and lists these specific California rule violations as the factual basis for the reciprocal USPTO discipline—illustrating types of conduct that can trigger reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the statutory/regulatory basis enabling the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline based on a state authority's disciplinary order.
